_comment: Candidate models found by pipeline/discover.py, awaiting review.
This file is hand-edited, like registry.json. discover.py only ever
appends new candidates and refreshes the fields of existing ones; it
never sets a status and never edits registry.json.
To review a row, set its status:
new       - not yet reviewed (what discover.py writes)
dismissed - not a sequence-to-function model, stop showing it
Add a 'note' to a row to record why. Dismissed rows stay here so the
judgement survives; they are counted, not re-surfaced.
matches_tracked_model flags a registry name appearing in the title.
It is a hint, not a verdict -- check before dismissing on it.

candidates.title: BEND 2.0: Benchmarking the Capabilities Needed to Design DNA
candidates.abstract: Genomic foundation models are increasingly used to propose DNA sequences and edits. But successful design requires capabilities that current benchmarks do not measure. Here we introduce BEND 2.0 (BENchmark for DNA language models), which tests how well models predict the effects of DNA changes and whether these predictions can guide sequence design. Across eight tasks built on five experimental datasets, we find that model choice and how representations are accessed both affect performance. candidates.title: IsoAlign: Isoform-Aware DNA-Protein Alignment via Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures
candidates.abstract: Genomic foundation models (GFMs) have emerged as a powerful paradigm for learning DNA sequence representations, yet existing self-supervised pretraining strategies overlook alternative splicing and underperform compared to specialized models. To address this gap, we introduce IsoAlign, a multimodal framework that grounds genomic pretraining in isoform-aware DNA-protein alignment to learn biologically meaningful representations. candidates.title: Localizing predictive concepts encoded in neural representations via hierarchical testing
candidates.abstract: Understanding which regulatory sequence motifs a genomic deep learning model has learned, with statistical error guarantees, is essential for trusting its use in downstream tasks such as variant effect prediction. Existing approaches to identifying which units in a trained network encode human- understandable concepts fall into two groups. Exploratory methods rank and visualize units but offer no statistical guarantee that the selected units are associated with the prediction target across the population of inputs. candidates.title: Accuracy is not compatibility: two Evo 2 checkpoints hinge on one FP8 matrix multiplication
candidates.abstract: FP8 formats specify how values are stored, not how products are summed; this gap can break checkpoints. Evo 2, a DNA language model, documents a Hopper FP8 requirement for its 1B and 40B checkpoints. On two Blackwell (sm_120) GPUs both fail the developers' forward test (the 7B passes); on an RTX 5070 Ti the 40B's next-base accuracy is 25.7%, near guessing. Greater accuracy breaks them, as BioNeMo saw for the 40B on Hopper: natively, 99.996% of one projection's outputs are correctly rounded (H100: about 30%), and fp32 accumulation of the same operands fails. candidates.abstract: Understanding the genetic changes that drove the evolution of human-specific traits is a central goal in biology. Changes in gene expression are thought to be a major source of phenotypic innovations, but identifying the underlying changes in cis-regulatory elements (CREs) along the human lineage has been difficult: functional data from great apes are scarce and unobtainable for extinct hominins, and pinpointing causal substitutions requires knowing which sequences determine CRE activity. candidates.title: Systematic mapping of the prokaryotic noncoding sequence space with a genomic language model
candidates.abstract: Prokaryotic genomes encode a vast repertoire of noncoding elements such as ribozymes, riboswitches, and CRISPR RNAs. The sequence-level diversity of these intergenic elements precludes alignment-based clustering that would enable annotation and discovery of novel noncoding RNA families. Here, we show that a genomic language model fine-tuned on prokaryotic intergenic sequences learns representations of noncoding elements from DNA sequence. We used these embeddings to organize 376 million intergenic regions from 1.3 terabase pairs of prokaryotic genomes and metagenomes into 5.14 million clusters

candidates.title: A genomic foundation model for interpreting human genetic diversity
candidates.abstract: Interpreting human genomes requires models that recognize shared biological functions while accounting for variation underlying traits, disease susceptibility and adaptation. Here we present hEVO, a genomic foundation model trained on 4.784 billion distinct haplotype sequences reconstructed from whole genome sequencing (WGS) data for 63,809 individuals selected from 550,237 samples across eight cohorts. candidates.title: Metagenomic contextualization of proteins with state space models
candidates.abstract: Genomic foundation models have emerged as powerful tools for learning representations of biological sequences, but existing approaches predominantly rely on Transformer architectures, whose quadratic attention complexity limits their ability to capture long-range genomic context. This limitation is particularly relevant for metagenomics, where sequencing data have increased more than 500-fold since 2011, generating increasingly large and diverse datasets. candidates.title: Predicting cell-state-specific gene regulation from DNA across species
candidates.abstract: DNA encodes the cell's phenotype, but the same DNA sequence is interpreted differently in every cell type, developmental stage, and activity state. Existing deep-learning models solve only half of this puzzle: sequence-to-function models read DNA but treat cell state as a fixed label, while single-cell foundation models represent cell state but not sequence. We developed Bolero, a sequence-to-function model whose parameters condition on atlas-scale cell-state embeddings and additional biological variables to predict cell-state-specific chromatin accessibility and transcript abundance from DNA.

candidates.title: Genomic foundation models do not yet boost common variant discovery beyond standard functional annotations
candidates.abstract: Genomic foundation models (GFMs) use large-scale AI to model genetic sequences and their influence on molecular phenotypes. While GFMs have shown promise in rare variant analysis, their utility for common variant discovery remains untested. Using the surrogate functional false discovery rate framework for functionally informed GWAS discovery, we compared standard functional annotations (baselineLD) with annotations derived from three leading GFMs: the sequence-to-function models AlphaGenome and Borzoi, and the genomic language model GPN-Star. candidates.title: Comprehensive molecular impact mapping of common and rare variants at GWAS loci
candidates.abstract: Deep learning sequence to function models can predict the molecular effects of genetic variants, but their predictions are limited to the cell types and assays they are trained on. Here we describe DNACipher, a deep learning model that predicts the effects of genetic variants across diverse biological contexts-including those not directly measured. DNACipher takes 524 kb of genome sequence as input and predicts variant effects across 38,582 cell type/assay combinations, > 6 times as many contexts as AlphaGenome. candidates.title: DeepD enables efficient genome modeling and controllable long-context sequence generation across domains of life
candidates.abstract: Genome foundation models hold great potential for advancing biological research, but modeling diverse complex genomes and generating controllable genome-scale sequences remain challenging. We present DeepD, a phylogeny-informed sparse mixture-of-experts model operating at single-nucleotide resolution over a 1-million-token context while reducing active computation. Pretrained on unselected whole-genome sequences across all domains of life, DeepD learns genic and intergenic sequence features and supports broad sequence-to-function prediction across species. candidates.title: A Training-Free Socket for DNA in Frozen Language Models
candidates.abstract: Connecting a DNA foundation model to a large language model (LLM) usually requires training a connector, and often the LLM too. We show that a closed-form map is enough for gene-level questions. Our method, the socket, fits one ridge regression (the plug) from frozen Evo 2 features to the host LLM's own representation of the gene's symbol, name, and description at an early layer. The plug's output replaces the hidden state at placeholder positions, and no gradient passes through the host. We test it on GeneHop, a five-way multiple-choice benchmark split by homology. candidates.title: GEMS (GWAS Effect Mechanisms via Sequence-to-Function): Unveiling cell type-specific mechanisms for GWAS variants
candidates.abstract: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have linked thousands of loci to common diseases, yet for non-coding variants, which constitute the vast majority of the signal, the cell types and states through which individual risk variants act remain largely unknown. candidates.title: DNA-LLM2Vec: Architecture-Aware Task-Conditioned Adaptation of Decoder DNA Foundation Models
candidates.abstract: Decoder DNA foundation models pretrain with dense next-token prediction and scale to long sequences, but their representations are directional. This is a poor fit for genomic tasks that need sequence context both upstream and downstream of a locus. Bidirectional masked-language-model encoders supply this context, but they pretrain more sparsely and scale less easily to long windows. candidates.title: A high-resolution protein-RNA binding atlas for structure-aware interaction prediction and post-transcriptional regulatory modeling
candidates.abstract: RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) control post-transcriptional gene expression by regulating RNA processing, localization, stability, and translation. However, our understanding of RNA regulation remains limited by the resolution, scale, and uniformity of available RBP binding maps. Here we introduce eclair CLIP (ecCLIP), a high-throughput CLIP-seq platform that combines endogenous protein tagging for uniform affinity capture with ligation-free library preparation to generate high-resolution RNA-protein binding profiles. candidates.abstract: Background: Sequence-to-function models predict regulatory perturbation responses, but their added value beyond established enhancer-gene predictors and across prediction tasks remains unclear. candidates.title: REMAG: recovery of eukaryotic genomes from metagenomic data using non-contrastive self-supervised learning
candidates.abstract: Metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) are central to exploring microbial communities. Yet, despite the relevance of protists and fungi to diverse ecosystems, eukaryotic MAG recovery lags behind that of prokaryotes. A major bottleneck is that most state-of-the-art binning pipelines exclusively rely on prokaryotic single-copy core gene reference databases and are optimized for smaller genomes. To address this gap, we present REMAG (Recovery of Eukaryotic MAGs), a tool designed to recover high-quality eukaryotic genomes suited for long-read metagenomic data. candidates.title: Alignment-Aware Genomic Coordinate Encoding for Long-Range DNA Modeling
candidates.abstract: Existing genomic foundation models (GFMs) are adept at capturing local, sequential dependencies in DNA. However, their architectures often struggle to efficiently model gene regulation features, such as sparse motifs and distal regulatory elements that operate beyond linear proximity. Moreover, standard positional encodings fail to fully exploit the reference genome coordinate system. candidates.title: What DNA Foundation Models Learn Beyond Sequence Composition
candidates.abstract: Do genomic foundation models (FMs) provide predictive information beyond simple sequence composition? We evaluate frozen representations from five DNA FMs against normalized k-mer frequencies across 57 genomic classification datasets and two exploratory gene-expression regression tasks. Simple k-mer features remain competitive with most models, whereas NTv3 shows a consistent advantage; the ranking is robust to globally fixed and multi-scale k-mer baselines and alternative downstream probes. candidates.abstract: Genomic language models generate long nucleotide continuations from short prefixes, exposing a direct route for studying training-sequence extraction through the generation interface. We present an output-only black-box attack on Evo 2 that selects convergent groups of repeated generations without gradients, token likelihoods, or training-corpus access during candidate selection. candidates.title: GLARE: Genomic Language model for Automated Repetitive Element classification
candidates.abstract: Reliable classification of transposable elements (TEs) is important for genome annotation and evolutionary analysis, yet remains challenging: TE families differ widely across taxa, reference databases label them inconsistently, and many TEs are represented only by degraded copies. We introduce GLARE (Genomic Language model for Automated Repetitive Element classification), a TE classifier built by fine-tuning a genomic language model on harmonized PanTEon and Repbase reference data to predict TE superfamily across 32 superfamilies in 11 orders. candidates.title: EvSpark: Lossless Speculative Decoding for Hybrid DNA Foundation Models
candidates.abstract: Hybrid DNA foundation models combine convolutional, recurrent, and attention layers, making speculative decoding more difficult than truncating a KV cache. candidates.abstract: Background Gene-level constraint and conservation scores are widely used to prioritise disease genes and to benchmark genomic language models. Purifying selection acts weakly on phenotypes manifesting after reproduction, so these scores are expected to carry less information about late-onset disease. An onset-dependent gradient has been demonstrated for human allele frequencies but not for the gene-level scores used in practice. candidates.abstract: RNA-based therapeutics increasingly rely on nuclease-resistant xeno-nucleic acids (XNAs), but engineering polymerases capable of reading and amplifying these non-canonical substrates remains a major challenge. Natural DNA polymerases cannot process C2' sugar modifications, and the complete structural determinants governing this limitation remain poorly understood, limiting rational design strategies. candidates.title: Systematic mapping of enhancers, silencers, and topological elements with prime editing deletion screens
candidates.abstract: Noncoding regulatory elements in the human genome can control gene expression through distinct mechanisms, including acting as enhancers, silencers, or topological elements. However, we lack tools to identify all such classes systematically and quantify their effects on gene expression in an endogenous genomic context. candidates.title: Fine-tuning genomic models on rare splicing events identifies a novel biomarker of TDP-43 pathology
candidates.abstract: Genomic foundation models (GFMs) are pretrained on large genomic datasets, but their ability to predict rare disease-associated events after fine-tuning remains unclear. We tested this using TDP-43 cryptic exons, well characterized splicing events linked to neurodegenerative disease that are poorly represented in standard annotations. We compared the state-of-the-art GFM AlphaGenome with OpenSpliceAI, a specialized splice site prediction model. candidates.title: Cerberus: bidirectional state space blocks improve accuracy and efficiency of regulatory sequence models
candidates.abstract: Sequence-to-function models predict regulatory activity and variant effects from DNA sequence alone, and leading models such as Borzoi compute long-range interactions with self-attention. The reference genome caps unique training sequences, and new assays add labels, not sequences. This constraint favors architectures that learn more from limited sequence diversity. candidates.title: Probing Genomic Foundation Models with Splice-Variant Perturbations
candidates.abstract: As benchmarks saturate, traditional validation methods fail to capture the probabilistic representations of genomic foundation models. This study probes self-supervised generalists (NTv3 650M, Evo2 40B, Genos 10B) alongside task-specific specialists (SpliceAI, AlphaGenome, Borzoi) using a mechanistically focused paradigm centered on expert-curated single-nucleotide substitutions within the splicing regions of the exon-rich OPA1 gene. candidates.title: RAGenome: Scaling Retrieval-Based Genomic Language Models to Long Contexts
candidates.abstract: The genome holds the blueprint that governs the biological properties of the cell. Consequently, advancing our knowledge of genomic function is crucial both for a broader understanding of biology and for continued biomedical advances. The success of large language models on natural language and protein sequences has motivated similar efforts on genomic data. candidates.title: REFinder: Mining new enzymes from metagenomes
candidates.abstract: Microbial metagenomes encode vast catalytic diversity, but recovering enzymes of novel, yet-undescribed functionality typically requires whole-community assembly plus a means of identifying active proteins ab initio. The first step of the task is compute-intensive and misses low-abundance sequences. The second is complicated by our inability to predict novel functions. candidates.title: RASTRO: Branching Point Decision-Making in Unitig Graphs
candidates.abstract: Motivation: De novo genome assembly relies on accurate path selection through complex graphs, yet unitig graph branching points remain a major ambiguity source. Multiple extensions may be equally plausible from topology alone, but sequence-level consistency of competing paths remains largely unexplored. Model: We introduce RASTRO, a reference-free framework for scoring candidate paths at unitig branching points using nucleotide sequence information. candidates.abstract: Sequence-to-function (S2F) models predict molecular phenotypes from DNA sequence and are increasingly applied to variant effect prediction (VEP), where the goal is to quantify how genetic variants alter gene expression. However, S2F model predictions are not uniformly reliable: accuracy varies substantially across variants, genes, and tissues, and current practice relies on crude magnitude thresholding to enrich for trustworthy predictions, which discards the majority of variants where S2F models could still provide signal. candidates.title: Evo2HiC: a multimodal foundation model for integrative analysis of genome sequence and architecture
candidates.abstract: Understanding how genome sequences shape three-dimensional (3D) genome architecture is fundamental to interpreting diverse biological processes. Although previous studies have shown that sequence information can predict 3D genome architecture, these models fall short in capturing cell type-specific structures because they are trained solely on sequence inputs. candidates.abstract: Genomic foundation models promise to infer regulatory consequences of genetic variants directly from DNA sequence, but how well these predictions translate to clinical utility remains unclear.
